page.layout: One page of text, no margin notes. Above the text: a decorative woodcut border (not transcribed). Then a centred title in capitals with a second line in lowercase, followed by a verse poem with a large woodcut initial at its start. Below the poem, the author's initials, set to the right. Printed page number at the top right.

main_text.head: IN GALLIAM BELLIS ciuilibus vexatam.
main_text.p: BEATA quondam Gallia, Misella nunc, in quam ruunt Noui malorum Turbines. Videto, quid sis! Non potes: Cùm cæca sis vt cæcitas. Audito, quid sis! Non potes: Cùm surda sis, vt surditas. Semper Tyrannis seruies, Nec te videbis liberam, Iugo subactam Cæsarum: Nam neminem Brutum paris. Et quos putas cives tuos, Tam se simul brutos amant, Tam se simul brutos volunt, Quàm bruta quæ sensu carent. Quod si forent bruti minus, Brutos haberes plurimos, Nullos haberes Cæsares.

page.notes: The first word is printed in small capitals, "EATA", with a large woodcut B as its initial; transcribed as BEATA. The printed "ciuilibus" is corrected to "civilibus" (consonant v). The first word "cæca" in the line "Cùm cæca sis" is hard to read in the scan and the letter forms may be a ligature; checked against the surrounding lines. Long s is rendered as s throughout, and the printed "sis" lines are copied as shown. No running head, catchword or signature is printed on this page.
